intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene (301057) on chromosome Xp21.1.

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: our experimental observations in humans and mice demonstrate that hemizygous mutations in CFAP47 can induce X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia
checks.explanation: The abstract does not use the name SPGFX3 (OMIM's label), but it states the causal link between hemizygous CFAP47 mutations and X-linked MMAF/asthenoteratozoospermia.

checks.claim: The CFAP47 gene is located on chromosome Xp21.1.
checks.evidence_quote: permitted the identification of a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene
checks.explanation: A deletion at Xp21.1 that removes the whole gene places CFAP47 at Xp21.1.

paragraphs.text: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is a form of primary male infertility. It is characterized by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF) (Liu et al., 2021).

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is a form of primary male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: Deleterious variants in X-linked CFAP47 induce asthenoteratozoospermia and primary male infertility.
checks.explanation: The title states that CFAP47 variants cause primary male infertility.

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is characterized by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF).
checks.evidence_quote: All men harboring hemizygous CFAP47 variants displayed typical MMAF phenotypes.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the phenotype as asthenoteratozoospermia with MMAF.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) reported 3 unrelated Chinese men with primary infertility and asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF). They also reported a man from an Australian cohort of men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. All of these men had typical MMAF phenotypes. Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed clearly reduced levels of CFAP47 in spermatozoa from the 3 Chinese men.

checks.evidence_quote: identified hemizygous missense variants in the X-linked CFAP47 in three unrelated Chinese individuals with MMAF

checks.claim: The 3 unrelated Chinese men reported by Liu et al. (2021) had asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF).

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) performed whole-exome sequencing in 3 unrelated Chinese men with MMAF and identified a hemizygous missense variant in the CFAP47 gene in each of them. The 3 variants were absent from human control population genome databases, and several bioinformatic tools predicted them to be deleterious. CFAP47 levels were clearly reduced in spermatozoa from all 3 men. In whole-exome sequencing data from a separate Australian cohort of men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia, Liu et al. (2021) identified a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion that removed the entire CFAP47 gene.

paragraphs.text: Liao et al. (2022) found that CFAP47 interacted with WDR87 in the midpiece of the sperm flagellum. In spermatozoa from a man with CFAP47 mutations, WDR87 expression was markedly reduced, with weak signals next to the sperm nuclei. The authors concluded that CFAP47 is needed to transport WDR87 during flagellar biogenesis, and that the 2 proteins form a complex involved in sperm tail assembly.

paragraphs.text: Based on findings in Cfap47-mutant mice, in which intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) restored fertility, Liu et al. (2021) suggested a good prognosis with ICSI for men with CFAP47-associated MMAF.
